SceneOutline: Develop Scene 4 as 3 connected beats, following the story direction.
Outline:
Purpose: Caelen wakes in the stone-walled pen, observing his captors shift from transactional indifference to active humiliation as he attempts a desperate social bluff to improve his conditions.

Viewpoint: Third-person limited (Caelen). The camera lingers on the grim texture of the enclosure—pale yellow light filtering through high slits, the rough skin of thirty others huddled in the shadows, and the heavy breathing of guards patrolling the perimeter.

Objective: Caelen must suppress his panic upon waking from the beat-induced unconsciousness. He assesses the immediate threat level: a masked man in purple undermines a scarred captive's authority while a guard strikes a distressed young woman. Caelen identifies an opening to intervene not through combat, but through a calculated social interaction with the guard, attempting to bluff his way into better treatment or at least less pain.

Meaningful Change: The narrative shifts from passive victimhood (transport) to active, albeit precarious, engagement within the slave pen. Caelen transitions from internal analysis of his status as "inventory" to external action, risking a moment of agency that contradicts his physical helplessness. He establishes a temporary dynamic with the guard where deception is the primary tool for survival.

Continuity Dependencies: This beat follows the cart ride ending in unconsciousness; Caelen is now alert but physically restrained by the collar and ropes. The scarred captive's standing must be visibly undermined by the man in purple to provide the context for Caelen’s intervention. The guard’s strike on the woman serves as the catalyst that forces Caelen to act, blending the established harshness of the world with his attempt at a quip-laden bluff.
Prose:
Caelen woke to the smell of wet stone and unwashed bodies. The cart’s suspension had groaned one last time before halting waking him up. He had gone in and out of sleep during the trip, but the trip couldn't have taken more than a few hours. They hadn't fed him nor given him any water. 

But it had been long enough for Mr. Halitosis to turn into Meeko. The two black eyes the guard that climbed into the cart was sporting made Caelen feel at least a little better about his own bruises. But it was with that thought that he realized that nothing really hurt. He was a bit sore, but nothing hurt like it did when he first woke up. Every bump in the road he had felt it. But he had eventually slept so either he had passed out or at some point the pain had gotten better.

Speaking in their throaty language Meeko formally known as Mr. Halitosis pulled Caelen to the edge of the cart and let him fall to the ground. Presumably deciding he didn't want to carry Caelen to wherever they were going he cut the binding on his feet. After beating the captive half to death, he likely figured there wasn't any fight left.  Which would explain the shock on his face as Meeko got his nose broken or at least returned to its formerly dislocation by the heel of a foot.  

When he awoke after the beating the next time Caelen found himself in a cell with thirty other captives, their forms where indistinct against the gloom. Some were wrapped in rags; others sat bare-chested, skin stained with soot or dried blood. A few eyes met his as he shifted his weight, testing the range of motion allowed.

The strangest part though was the positioning of the others in the cell. He was laying at the cell door. Caelen could only assume in the exact location he was dropped. As he uncurled his cramped muscles he hurt but not nearly enough. He had just been kicked unconscious twice in a short period, but nothing was broken, breathing only gave a slight twinge of pain and all the muscles so far had worked without cramping. He was in much better shape than he expected.
 
He tried to suppress the rising panic. Fear would get you beaten; indifference might keep you alive for another day. He focused on observation instead of reaction. On the other side of the bars near the cell door stood two guards in dull uniforms, spears resting casually against their shoulders. Their faces were hidden, shadowed by hoods. They moved without urgency, watching not him but someone deeper inside the pen.

On the far side Inside, a masked man in purple leaned over a scarred captive seated on an overturned crate. The scarred man’s posture betrayed exhaustion, yet he spoke with an air of authority that the purple-masked figure openly undermined. He flipped pages of a ledger, his black-tipped cane tapping rhythmically against the stone floor, as if conducting some unseen orchestra of humiliation.

Then came the strike.

A guard stepped forward and swung his staff hard across the shoulders of a young woman crouched near the back wall. She cried out—a sound torn between pain and terror—before collapsing onto her knees. The guard didn’t even look at her after the blow, stepping back to face Caelen’s direction.

Her scream caught in his chest like a stone dropped into water. Caelen froze for a heartbeat, then forced himself to move before someone else took notice of his sudden alertness. If he could play the role of the helpful idiot long enough, maybe they’d let him breathe easier. Maybe even earn something more than survival.

He stood slowly, letting his eyes meet the guard’s masked face. "Hey," Caelen said, keeping his voice low but steady, though every word felt alien on his tongue. "You hit her hard."

The guard scoffed, raising the butt of his staff again. Caelen kept talking, bluffing with a calmness he didn't feel. "Look at that. I’m just guessing here, right? You know how it is out there. Bad guys always pick the easiest targets first." He paused, letting the silence stretch thin. "Maybe if you give her a second to catch her breath, she won’t run screaming next time something goes wrong. That’s what happens when you don’t account for variables, yeah?"

The guard hesitated, then lowered his staff slightly. Caelen had bought him a few seconds—and maybe a little space.
